newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi Guard pilot killed in copter crash.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi Guard pilot killed in copter crash.

text.p: A Mississippi National Guard pilot was killed when his helicopter plunged into a wooded area and burned while on a training flight, a National Guard official said Wednesday.

Chief Warrant Officer Bradford Green, 49, of Amory, Mississippi, was killed when the Kiowa Warrior helicopter went down Tuesday about six miles (10 km) south of Beaumont, said Maj. Dennis Smith, a spokesman for the National Guard training base at Camp Shelby.
"The unit was conducting a reconnaissance flight with nine other aircraft during night tactical operations," he said.
The other pilot on the helicopter, Capt. Christopher Bobo, 35, of Muscle Shoals, Alabama, suffered minor injuries, Smith said. Both men were members of Company H, 1st Battalion, 185th Aviation.
Green was a decorated veteran of the Vietnam War, he said.
Smith said the cause of the crash was uncertain. A team was sent from the Army Safety Centre at Fort Rucker, Alabama to investigate.
"The team will first look at the possibility of mechanical failure," Smith said. The other aircraft returned to base without incident.
